title: Allow Jensen integrity checks without POSIX resource (no κ)
body:
## Summary

The frozen PR5614 entry imports POSIX `resource` before selecting `--integrity-only`, so even file authentication fails when that module is unavailable. This opt-in, source-authenticated adapter moves the import into the retained child guard:

```diff
-import resource
 def child_limits():
+    import resource
     resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (512*1024*1024,512*1024*1024))
```

Claim type: scoped implementation-preservation proof with finite conformance. The complete original integrity checks and stdout are retained, and scientific execution still requires its original guard. This is a portability improvement with no new mathematical result, numerical audit, supplier admission or kappa. Predecessor files and the selected frontier are unchanged.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Chris R / Clear1nsight for PR5614's entire authentication/scientific entry and hypothetical compiler benchmark, with Hexapode, Ali Romman, thu-nmrc, GamingPuzzled, DreamingOfClouds, zxv, Cao Yifan, Jacob Alan Sussman, Cinna Davis and its retained lineage.

## Evidence

Before: the actual frozen entry raises `ModuleNotFoundError` at `resource` under a missing-module control. After: the new entry completes all original integrity checks without requesting that import and prints `PASS_P104_JENSEN_BENCHMARK_INTEGRITY_ONLY_NO_SCIENCE`.

Both normal and optimized checks print `PASS_JENSEN_LAZY_RESOURCE` with identical generated hash-bound receipts. Evidence includes exact AST relocation, complete original stdout equality, identical 536870912-byte guard arguments, missing-module/denied-limit failure propagation, five distinct custody mutations and two unsupported-argument controls. All 53 retained files are declared live inputs.

Reproduce from the repository root with standard-library CPython 3.12:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -B research/jensen-resource-lazy/run.py --integrity-only
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/jensen-resource-lazy/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/jensen-resource-lazy/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/jensen-resource-lazy
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/jensen-resource-lazy --check-source-history
```

All pass locally at head `1f99fce085ee6e0a8997b43dcfbd889d9fdf1dc1`. Another CPython 3.12 executable may replace the displayed path. Committed-byte/source-history checks cover 59 files; official export integrity and all 53 declared inputs pass. Both complete checks also pass from a read-only Git-free export with spaces in its path and empty executable PATH, in 0.094 and 0.109 seconds. All 60 export files, including the export manifest, retain their bytes and modes. These are check durations, not speedup claims. Local platform: CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

Native Windows execution and OS enforcement of the resource limit are unrun. The missing-module and guard-argument controls establish this specific import boundary. Full scientific execution remains dependent on the retained POSIX subprocess API; no unguarded fallback is supplied. Module-global inspection, traceback/source positions, import timing and external replacement of the old global resource binding are outside preservation scope.

No predecessor mathematical replay, selected cold replay, native/compiler/physical admission, Lean or Docker run was performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The existing mathematical claims remain their authors' evidence.

## Open next questions

Run both committed VERIFY commands in a native Windows CPython 3.12 source export. This would test the remaining platform behavior without changing the scientific contract.

## Related open work

No other open PR studying the PR5614 integrity entry or this missing-resource boundary was found in the submission refresh. Completion refresh inspected all 96 account open PRs, including the ten other PRs created since the advance CLAIM. None studies this retained integrity entry or computes a competing result for it. No extra computation was run to check another contribution. General P104 compiler and supplier proposals concern different contracts and no numerical comparison is made here.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/jensen-resource-lazy)`, passed at exact head `1f99fce085ee6e0a8997b43dcfbd889d9fdf1dc1` in [run 41556474574](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41556474574). The completed checks were read once; run metadata confirms completed success and the matching head. Hosted replay executes both registered normal and optimized commands.

Both registered commands, direct entry, committed-byte/source-history and read-only Git-free export checks also pass locally. CI certifies execution of the registered finite checks and source bindings, not native Windows behavior, OS enforcement of the resource limit, independent mathematical acceptance or a formal proof-kernel theorem. No failed or waived check remains.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19363539). Current canonical main and governing guidance were refreshed before publication.
